newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Viag targets higher profit, investment.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Viag targets higher profit, investment.

text.p: Munich-based diversified industrial group Viag AG said it expected 1996 pre-tax profits to be at least equal to those in 1995, while group turnover for the year was expected to rise.
It also confirmed that it was interested in buying stakes in utility groups including the Swiss concern Elektrowatt, and promised several billion marks of investment over the next five years.

Speaking at a news briefing late on Wednesday, Viag chief executive Georg Obermeier said he expected 1996 profits would at least match those of the year before. "The pre-tax profit will be at least equal to that in 1995 and even a little better,"
For 1997, Obermeier said Viag could expect turnover and profits a bit better than in 1996.
In 1995, Viag made a pre-tax profit of 2.2 billion marks ($1.4 billion) on turnover of 41.9 billion, a figure that Obermeier expects to have risen to around 45 billion in 1996.
He said Viag's original plan to have its energy division account for just 50 percent of profits, with other activities taking up the other half, would not be realised in the medium term.
Energy would continue to contribute at least 60 percent to profits in five years time, he estimated.
Shares in Viag rose 1.20 marks to 602.50 on the news on a largely flat Frankfurt bourse.
Obermeier said Viag was expecting investments over the next five years to amount to several billion marks, to be spent on acquisitions, cooperation and the "usual" investments.
Among possible purchases, Viag confirmed it was interested in increasing its stake in the German utility Bewag AG and was also interested in Swiss group Elektrowatt.
Viag along with German diversified utility Veba AG already has a 10 percent stake in Bewag, which is still majority-owned by the state of Berlin.
An offer from the two for the 25.8 percent stake up for sale by the Berlin state could be made as soon as Friday, Obermeier indicated.
Other groups, including British electricity generator PowerGen Plc, have also expressed an interest in Bewag.
Obermeier confirmed that Viag was interested in taking a stake in Elektrowatt, saying Viag saw the Swiss energy sector as particularly attractive.
Shares in the Swiss industrial and utility group have risen recently on speculation that bank group CS Holding was to sell its 44.9 percent stake by the year-end.
